senses.gloss: m. (Parpel noun of דקק; cmp. דַּקִּיק a. רַּעְדֵּק) tender, young, small; esp. pupil of a primary class.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 3:19">Targ. Job III, 19</cite>.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 66a:8">B. Mets. 66ᵃ</cite> <he>ד׳ קרעיה גברא רבא וכ׳</he> was it a child that destroyed the note? A great man &c.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 66a:9">Ib.</cite> <he>ד׳ קרעיה דכולי עלמא וכ׳</he> it was a beginner in learning that tore it, for, in civil law, all people are beginners &c.—Pl. <cite ref="D01048"><he>דַּרְדְּקִין</he></cite>, <cite ref="D01049"><he>דַּרְדְּקֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 30:1">Targ. Job XXX, 1</cite> <he>ד׳ מיני</he> my juniors; a. e.—B. Mets. l. c.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 21a:10">B. Bath. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>מקרי ד׳</he> teacher of primaries (Bible teacher); <cite ref="Bekhorot 46a:2">Bekh. 46ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 111b:20">Keth. 111ᵇ</cite> <he>מקרי ד׳ דר״ל</he> the teacher of Resh Lakish’s children.
